newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria crisis hits LDC debt in London.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria crisis hits LDC debt in London.

text.p: A political crisis in Bulgaria took a heavy toll on the country's Brady debt in London, with prices falling in the political vacuum brought about by Saturday's resignation of the country's prime minister.
Congress delegates were preparing to vote in Sofia on Monday for a new premier and party leader after Prime Minister Zhan Videnov quit in a surprise move on Saturday.
"Bulgaria opened weaker on the resignation," said one east European debt trader here. "It is now trading between one and 1-1/2 points weaker than where it closed but turnover is tiny."
Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR, which represent pure Bulgarian debt, opened at 50-00 bid-side after closing on Friday at 52-00.
They edged back to 50-3/4 by 1135 GMT but dealers said they were gapping up and down.

The market, used to such large swings in Bulgarian debt prices, is less worried about Videnov's chances of getting reelected than about how to eliminate the uncertainty that wiped two percent off the country's debt prices in early trading.
"People are concerned with the IMF, the currency board and what's happening to the lev," said John Gibbens, East Europe analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "People want stability."
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has been pressing Bulgaria to undertake painful reform measures and implement a tough monetary regime to stave off economic collapse.

Its failure to meet reform targets, including privatisation and shutting down loss-making industries, has caused the suspension of IMF and World Bank funding, and the lev has all but collapsed in the interim.

But Gibbens took heart from the fact that the main candidates for the premier's post appeared to back the idea of the currency board that aims to bring economic stability by fixing the exchange rate for the lev.
The board should be set up early next year.

The rest of the emerging debt market remained moribund at the start of the Christmas week. Russian debt prices were unmoved by President Boris Yeltsin's return to work, and Latin paper was steady to a touch weaker.
Players welcomed news that some of the hostages held in the Japanese embassy in Peru had been released but Peruvian debt, only lightly traded in London, showed little reaction.
"Apart from Bulgaria, everyone's off eating mince pies," one trader said.
Russian dollar Vnesh loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were quoted flat at 77-1/2; Brazil C bonds BR8D14=RR were off 1/4 at 73-00; and Peru Citi paper PEFLG91=RR was flat at 114-1/4.
The J.P. Morgan composite emerging market bond index was up 0.49 percent at 141.54 after the close of play on Friday. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
